items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: I played with Frankie -- with Frankie before I played with Eddie Hayward

ctx.x: He copied Frankie -- he was crazy about Frankie [illegible]. He would play all them solos that Frankie -- and things like that. And then -- at the end of that -- we -- we joined Steve Rebb's (PHONETIC) band. STEVE REBB
That band joined Steve Rebb (PHONETIC). That's how Steve Rebb (PHONETIC) formed.

items.q: The interviewer mentions 'Tromb' in the context of a recording ('Trombology'), but the interviewee (Vic Dickenson) does not respond or provide any personal connection or interaction with this person in the provided text.

ctx.x: That's "Tromb..." I don't know whether it is or not. But he didn't sound... He sounded as modern in them times... In fact, that sounds good now, you know, if you play it. So what are you going to do with that? Right?
That's playing with a lot of changes. So that was already pretty much a way of playing then. Sometimes people seem to think that playing on changes didn't come in until later on...
